title.zh: 卷八十四 列傳第十四: 耶律沙 耶律抹只 蕭幹 耶律善補 耶律海里
title.en: Volume 84 Biographies 14: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan, Yelu Shanbu, Yelu Haili
title.raw: 卷八十四 列傳第十四: 耶律沙 耶律抹只 蕭幹 耶律善補 耶律海里 Volume 84 Biographies 14: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan, Yelu Shanbu, Yelu Haili

sentences.zh: 耶律沙 耶律抹只 蕭幹附:討古 耶律善補 耶律海裏

translations.literal: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan with appendix: Taogu, Yelu Shanbu, Yelu Haili
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Sha, Yelu Mozhi, Xiao Gan, appended biography Taogu, Yelu Shanbu, and Yelu Haili

sentences.zh: 耶律沙

translations.literal: Yelu Sha
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Sha

sentences.zh: 耶律沙，字安隱。

translations.literal: Yelu Sha, courtesy name Anyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Sha, whose courtesy name was Anyin.

sentences.zh: 其先嘗相遙輦氏。

translations.literal: His ancestors had once been ministers to the Yaolian clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had once served as ministers to the Yaolian clan.

sentences.zh: 應歷間，累官南府宰相。

translations.literal: During the Yingli reign, through repeated offices he reached Southern Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingli era he rose through successive posts to become Chancellor of the Southern Office.

sentences.zh: 景宗即位，總領南面邊事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he took overall charge of southern frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong acceded, Sha was placed in overall charge of affairs along the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 保寧間，宋攻河東，沙將兵救之，有功，加守太保。

translations.literal: During Baoning, Song attacked Hedong; Sha led troops to rescue it, had merit, and was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baoning period, when the Song attacked Hedong, Sha led troops to its relief and distinguished himself; he was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初，宋復北侵，沙將兵由間道至白馬嶺，阻大澗遇敵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, Song again invaded north; Sha led troops by a hidden route to White Horse Ridge, blocked by a great ravine where he met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianheng era, when the Song again pressed northward, Sha marched by a concealed route to White Horse Ridge, where a deep ravine brought him face to face with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 沙與諸將欲待後軍至而戰，冀王敵烈、監軍耶律抹只等以為急擊之便，沙不能奪。

translations.literal: Sha and the generals wished to wait until the rear army arrived before fighting; the Prince of Ji, Dilie, the army supervisor Yelu Mozhi, and others held that a swift attack would be advantageous, and Sha could not overrule them.
translations.idiomatic: Sha and his fellow commanders wanted to hold action until the rear guard came up; the Prince of Ji, Dilie, the army supervisor Yelu Mozhi, and others argued for an immediate assault, and Sha could not prevail against them.

sentences.zh: 敵烈等以先鋒渡澗，未半，為宋人所擊，兵潰。

translations.literal: Dilie and the others led the vanguard across the ravine; before they were halfway over, they were struck by the Song and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie and his colleagues took the vanguard across the ravine, but before they were even halfway over the Song struck them and the force broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 敵烈及其子蛙哥、沙之子德裏、令穩都敏、詳穩唐筈等五將俱沒。

translations.literal: Dilie, his son Wage, Sha's son Deli, Lingwen Dumin, Xiangwen Tanghua, and five generals in all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Dilie, his son Wage, Sha's son Deli, the lingwen Dumin, the xiangwen Tanghua, and three other commanders—five generals in all—were killed.

sentences.zh: 會北院大王耶律斜軫兵至，萬矢俱發，敵軍始退。

translations.literal: Just then the Northern Chancellor Yelu Xiezhen's troops arrived; ten thousand arrows flew together, and the enemy army only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the Northern Chancellor Yelu Xiezhen arrived with his troops; when ten thousand arrows flew as one, the enemy at last drew back.

sentences.zh: 沙將趨太原，會漢駙馬都尉盧俊來奔，言太原已陷，遂勒兵還。

translations.literal: Sha was about to hurry to Taiyuan when the Han Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Lu Jun came fleeing to him, saying Taiyuan had already fallen, and he thereupon reined in the army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sha was pressing toward Taiyuan when the Han Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Lu Jun came over to his side and reported that Taiyuan had already fallen; Sha thereupon turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 宋乘銳侵燕，沙與戰於高梁河，稍卻；

translations.literal: The Song, riding their momentum, invaded Yan; Sha fought them at Gaoliang River and fell back slightly;
translations.idiomatic: The Song, emboldened by their momentum, thrust into Yan; Sha met them at the Gaoliang River and gave ground;

sentences.zh: 遇耶律休哥及斜軫等邀擊，敗宋軍。

translations.literal: he encountered Yelu Xiuge and Xiezhen and others intercepting and striking, and defeated the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: but then Yelu Xiuge, Xiezhen, and others cut across their path and routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 宋主宵遁，至涿州，微服乘驢車，間道而走。

translations.literal: The Song ruler fled by night; reaching Zhuozhou, in plain dress he rode a donkey cart and escaped by byways.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor fled under cover of night; reaching Zhuozhou, he went in disguise in a donkey cart along back roads to safety.

sentences.zh: 上以功釋前過。

translations.literal: The emperor, for this merit, released his earlier fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned his earlier failures in light of this success.

sentences.zh: 是年，復從韓匡嗣伐宋，敗績，帝欲誅之，以皇后營救得免。

translations.literal: That year he again followed Han Kuangsi in attacking Song, suffered defeat, and the emperor wished to execute him; through the empress's intercession he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he again joined Han Kuangsi in a campaign against the Song and met with defeat; the emperor meant to put him to death, but the empress pleaded for him and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 睿智皇后稱制，召賜几杖，以優其老。

translations.literal: When the Sagacious Empress Dowager held the regency, she summoned him and bestowed a folding stool and staff to honor his age.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sagacious Empress Dowager assumed the regency, she summoned him and granted him a folding stool and staff as marks of esteem for his advanced years.

sentences.zh: 復從伐宋，敗劉廷讓、李敬源之軍，賜賚優渥。

translations.literal: He again followed in attacking Song, defeated the armies of Liu Tingrang and Li Jingyuan, and received lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field once more against the Song, routed the forces of Liu Tingrang and Li Jingyuan, and received a generous grant of rewards.

sentences.zh: 統和六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tonghe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Tonghe reign.

sentences.zh: 耶律抹只

translations.literal: Yelu Mozhi
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Mozhi

sentences.zh: 蕭幹，小字項烈，字婆典，北府宰相敵魯之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Gan, childhood name Xianglie, courtesy name Podian, son of the Northern Chancellor Diru.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gan, whose childhood name was Xianglie and courtesy name Podian, was the son of the Northern Chancellor Diru.

sentences.zh: 性質直。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and plain.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was forthright and plain-spoken.

sentences.zh: 初，察割之亂，其黨胡古只與幹善，使人召之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Chagai's rebellion, his partisan Huguzhi was on good terms with Gan and sent someone to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chagai's rebellion, one of his partisans, Huguzhi, who was on friendly terms with Gan, sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 幹曰：「吾豈能從逆臣！

translations.literal: Gan said: "How could I follow a rebellious minister!
translations.idiomatic: Gan replied, "How could I follow a traitor!

sentences.zh: 」縛其人送壽安王。

translations.literal: He bound the man and sent him to the Prince of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: He bound the envoy and sent him to the Prince of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 賊平，上嘉其忠，拜群牧都林牙。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the emperor praised his loyalty and appointed him Chief Forest Master of the Herds.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, the emperor commended his loyalty and appointed him Chief Forest Master of the Herds.

sentences.zh: 復以伐烏古功，遷北府宰相，改突呂不部節度使。

translations.literal: Again, for merit in attacking the Wugu, he was transferred to Northern Chancellor and made Military Commissioner of the Tulübu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Northern Chancellor for his service against the Wugu and made Military Commissioner of the Tulübu tribe.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初，宋伐河東，乘勝侵燕，詔幹拒之，戰於高梁河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, Song attacked Hedong and, pressing their advantage, invaded Yan; the emperor ordered Gan to resist them, and he fought at Gaoliang River.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianheng, when the Song attacked Hedong and, riding their victory, pressed into Yan, the court ordered Gan to hold them off; he gave battle at the Gaoliang River.

sentences.zh: 耶律沙退走，幹與耶律休哥等並力戰敗之，上手敕慰勞。

translations.literal: Yelu Sha had retreated; Gan together with Yelu Xiuge and others joined forces, defeated the enemy, and the emperor sent a hand-written edict to console and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Sha had already fallen back, but Gan joined Yelu Xiuge and others in a combined assault that broke the enemy; the emperor sent a personal edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 自是每征伐必參決軍事。

translations.literal: From this time on, in every campaign he was sure to take part in deciding military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he took part in every major military decision.

sentences.zh: 加政事令。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Chief of Political Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Chief of Political Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，宋兵圍瓦橋，夜襲我營，幹及耶律勻骨戰卻之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Song troops besieged Wagiao; at night they raided our camp, and Gan together with Yelu Jungu fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Song forces besieged Wagiao and raided the Liao camp by night, Gan and Yelu Jungu drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時皇后以父呼幹。

translations.literal: At the time the empress addressed Gan as "Father."
translations.idiomatic: The empress addressed him as "Father."

sentences.zh: 及後為皇太后稱制，幹數條奏便宜，多見聽用。

translations.literal: Later, when she became empress dowager regent, Gan repeatedly submitted proposals of practical benefit, and many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when she ruled as empress dowager, Gan submitted one practical proposal after another, and many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 統和四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tonghe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Tonghe reign.

sentences.zh: 侄討古。

translations.literal: Nephew Taogu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew was Taogu.

translations.literal: 〈Appended〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 討古

translations.literal: Taogu
translations.idiomatic: Taogu

sentences.zh: 討古，字括寧，性忠簡。

translations.literal: Taogu, courtesy name Kuoning, nature loyal and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Taogu, whose courtesy name was Kuoning, was loyal and unassuming by nature.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，始入侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he first entered attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yingli era he first entered palace service.

sentences.zh: 會冀王敵烈、宣徽使海思謀反，討古與耶律阿列密告於上，上嘉其忠，詔尚樸謹公主。

translations.literal: It happened that the Prince of Ji, Dilie, and the Xuanhui Commissioner Haisi plotted rebellion; Taogu together with Yelu Alie secretly reported to the emperor, who praised his loyalty and ordered him to marry Princess Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ji, Dilie, and the Xuanhui Commissioner Haisi conspired rebellion, Taogu and Yelu Alie reported them in secret; the emperor praised their loyalty and married Taogu to Princess Pujin.

sentences.zh: 保寧末，為南京統軍使。

translations.literal: At the end of Baoning he became Southern Capital Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Baoning he was made Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乾亨初，宋侵燕，討古與北院大王奚底拒之，不克，軍潰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianheng, Song invaded Yan; Taogu together with the Northern Chancellor Xidi resisted them, could not overcome them, and the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianheng, when the Song invaded Yan, Taogu and the Northern Chancellor Xidi tried to hold them off but failed and their army broke in rout.

sentences.zh: 討古等不敢復戰，退屯清河。

translations.literal: Taogu and the others did not dare fight again and withdrew to encamp at Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Taogu and his colleagues dared not give battle again and fell back to encamp at Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其敗，遣使責之曰：「卿等不嚴偵候，用兵無法，遇敵即敗，奚以將為！

translations.literal: The emperor heard of their defeat and sent an envoy to rebuke them, saying: "You did not keep strict watch, employed troops without method, and were defeated as soon as you met the enemy—how can you serve as generals!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of the defeat, he sent an envoy to rebuke them: "You kept poor watch, handled your troops without discipline, and broke the moment you met the enemy—what sort of commanders are you!

sentences.zh: 」討古懼。

translations.literal: Taogu was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Taogu was terrified.

sentences.zh: 頃之，援兵至，討古奮力以敗宋軍。

translations.literal: Before long reinforcements arrived; Taogu exerted himself with force and defeated the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long reinforcements arrived, and Taogu fought with renewed vigor to rout the Song army.

sentences.zh: 上釋其罪，降為南京侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: The emperor released his guilt and demoted him to Commander of the Southern Capital Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned him but reduced him to Commander of the Southern Capital Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Qianheng.

sentences.zh: 耶律善補

translations.literal: Yelu Shanbu
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Shanbu

sentences.zh: 耶律善補，字瑤升，孟父楚國王之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Shanbu, courtesy name Yaosheng, descendant of the younger father, King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Shanbu, whose courtesy name was Yaosheng, was a descendant of the younger line of the King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 純謹有才智。

translations.literal: Pure, careful, and possessed of talent and wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: He was conscientious, prudent, and gifted with ability.

sentences.zh: 景宗即位，授千牛衛大將軍，遷大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, he was appointed Grand General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and transferred to Military Commissioner of Datong Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne, he was made Grand General of the Thousand-Ox Guard and then Military Commissioner of the Datong Army.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，韓匡嗣與耶律沙將兵由東路進，善補以南京統軍使由西路進。

translations.literal: When they attacked Song, Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha led troops in by the eastern route; Shanbu as Southern Capital Commander-in-Chief advanced by the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the Song, Han Kuangsi and Yelu Sha advanced along the eastern route while Shanbu, as Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Capital, moved up the western route.

sentences.zh: 善補聞匡嗣失利，斂兵還。

translations.literal: Shanbu heard that Kuangsi had suffered defeat and gathered in his troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanbu learned that Kuangsi had been defeated, he drew his troops back.

sentences.zh: 乾亨末，與宋軍戰於滿城，為伏兵所圍，斜軫救之獲免。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianheng he fought Song troops at Mancheng, was surrounded by ambush troops, and Xiezhen rescued him so he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianheng he fought the Song at Mancheng, was caught in an ambush, and was saved only when Xiezhen came to his relief.

sentences.zh: 以失備，大杖決之。

translations.literal: For lack of preparedness he was sentenced to heavy cudgeling.
translations.idiomatic: For his lack of preparedness he was sentenced to a severe beating.

sentences.zh: 統和初，為惕隱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe he became tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tonghe he was made tiyin.

sentences.zh: 會宋來侵，善補為都元帥逆之，不敢戰，故嶺西州郡多陷，罷惕隱。

translations.literal: When Song came to invade, Shanbu as supreme commander went to meet them but did not dare fight; therefore many prefectures and districts west of the passes fell, and he was removed as tiyin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song invaded again, Shanbu went out as supreme commander to meet them but would not give battle; many districts west of the passes therefore fell, and he was dismissed from the office of tiyin.

sentences.zh: 以其叔安端有匡輔世宗功，上湣之，征善補為南府宰相，遷南院大王。

translations.literal: Because his uncle Anduan had the merit of supporting and assisting Emperor Shizong, the emperor pitied him and summoned Shanbu to be Southern Chancellor, transferring him to Great King of the Southern Office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his uncle Anduan had helped secure Emperor Shizong's succession, the court showed him favor: Shanbu was recalled to serve as Southern Chancellor and promoted to Great King of the Southern Office.

sentences.zh: 會再舉伐宋，欲攻魏府，召眾集議。

translations.literal: When they again raised troops to attack Song and wished to assault Weizhou, he summoned the host to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: On a later campaign against the Song, when the court planned to strike Weizhou, he called the commanders together for counsel.

sentences.zh: 將士以魏城無備，皆言可攻。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, because Weizhou was undefended, all said it could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men, seeing Weizhou undefended, all urged an assault.

sentences.zh: 善補曰：「攻固易，然城大叵量，若克其城，士卒貪俘掠，勢必不可遏。

translations.literal: Shanbu said: "The attack is indeed easy, yet the city is large beyond measure; if we take it, the soldiers will be greedy for captives and plunder, and the momentum will surely be impossible to restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Shanbu said, "The assault would be easy enough, but the city is vast; if we took it, the men would gorge on captives and loot, and the rush would be impossible to hold in check.

sentences.zh: 且傍多巨鎮，各出援兵，內有重敵，何以當之？

translations.literal: Moreover, nearby are many great strongholds; each will send relief troops—within we would have a heavy enemy; how could we withstand it?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, great fortified towns lie all around; each would send relief, and we would face powerful enemies on every side—how could we stand against them?

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 善補性懦，守靜。

translations.literal: Shanbu's nature was timid; he kept to quietude.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Shanbu was timid and preferred quiet.

sentences.zh: 凡征討，憚攻戰，急還，以故戰多不利。

translations.literal: In every campaign he dreaded fighting, hurried back, and for this reason battles were often unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he shrank from battle and withdrew at the first opportunity, and for this reason his engagements usually went badly.

sentences.zh: 年七十四卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 耶律海裏

translations.literal: Yelu Haili
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Haili

sentences.zh: 論曰：當高梁、朔州之捷，偏裨之將如沙與抹只，既因休哥、斜軫類見其功，所謂失之東隅，收之桑榆。

translations.literal: The discussion says: At the victories at Gaoliang and Shuozhou, subordinate generals such as Sha and Mozhi, having through Xiuge, Xiezhen, and the like been seen for their merit, exemplify what is called losing at the eastern corner yet gaining at the mulberry and elm.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: At the victories at Gaoliang and Shuozhou, subordinate commanders such as Sha and Mozhi—though they had first been disgraced—won distinction alongside men like Xiuge and Xiezhen; this is truly a case of losing at dawn yet making good the loss at dusk.

sentences.zh: 若蕭幹、海裏拒察割之招，討古告海思之變，則不止有戰功而已。

translations.literal: As for Xiao Gan and Haili refusing Chagai's summons, and Taogu reporting Haisi's plot, they possessed more than battlefield merit alone.
translations.idiomatic: As for Xiao Gan and Haili, who refused Chagai's enticements, and Taogu, who exposed Haisi's conspiracy—their worth lay in more than battlefield success alone.

sentences.zh: 其視善補畏懦，豈不優哉！

translations.literal: Compared with Shanbu's timid cowardice, are they not superior!
translations.idiomatic: Set beside Shanbu's timid caution, were they not plainly the better men!
